In the thread https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/113489-new-members/topic/Introducing.20myself.3A.20Lasse.20Rempe/with/626587633 we started discussing complex analysis - particularly the Cauchy integral theorem - in Mathlib. I suggest that we continue the discussion here.

@Junyan Xu @Lars Kuehne

#maths > Multivariate complex analysis @ 💬 was the previous thread I believe
(but this channel probably makes more sense)

I'll note that the residue theorem is usually proved in a first complex analysis course without requiring van Kampen's theorem (and Cauchy's theorem without requiring such things as Étale spaces). If these are available and give an easier proof/ appropriately more general statements etc, I am all for using them, but I worry that it may delay things indefinitely ...

I like to mention here my lean-CA project that is devoted to fundamental complex analysis not yet in Mathlib (or, later, in TauCeti). Here is a mathematical synopsis. I tried to get the project accepted into Palomar, but it was judged to be too elementary for that space. It could be turned into a PR for TauCeti; I might have done that already, but got distracted. On the other hand, it could be adopted and adapted (adapted as much as you like) into this broader "Lasse Rempe" CA project. All the proofs in my lean-CA project were produced by LLM; primarily Claude and GPT.

The etale space approach allows to define integration along any continuous path (or singular 1-chain) via path lifting to a covering space, rendering the polygonal approximation as suggested by @Sébastien Gouëzel unnecessary; however this only works for 1-chains and doesn't obviously generalize to higher dimensions, where you may have to use smooth approximations and show well-definedness using smooth homotopies.

The ability to work with continuous paths in contour integrals would be quite convenient and help eliminate the trick currently in use in PrimeNumberTheorem+ and possibly sphere packing repos to produce smooth curves following a contour by making the speed zero at corners. It would also be easier to deform the contours if the homotopies are not required to be smooth.

Van Kampen and corollaries are available now in TauCeti, which should eventually be upstreamed to Mathlib. If you're only interested in simple closed curves as contours then you can of course construct explicit homotopy from the s.s.c. to small loops around punctures inside it. Here instead of computing winding numbers you need to exhibit a disk bounded by the s.s.c. that contains the punctures.

To start, perhaps an easy goal is the minimum modulus principle?
(we already have the maximum one)

The method of integration using étalé spaces sounds very promising. I have one request, which is that we allow non-abelian coefficients whenever possible (that is, before passing from lists of paths to 1-chains).
